Put psi(lambda)=lambda^2/(2L_0^2), e_0(lambda)=(cosh psi,sinh psi,0,0), e_1(lambda)=(sinh psi,cosh psi,0,0), and z(lambda)=(integral_0^lambda cosh psi(s) ds,integral_0^lambda sinh psi(s) ds,0,0), so z'=e_0 and eta(z',z')=-1. Define Phi(lambda,xi,y,zeta)=z(lambda)+xi e_1(lambda)+y e_2+zeta e_3. On a sufficiently small open coordinate box around0 this is injective with smooth inverse and N=1+k(lambda)xi>0, where k(lambda)=lambda/L_0^2; its pullback metric is -N^2 d lambda^2+d xi^2+dy^2+d zeta^2. The unit field n=N^-1 partial_lambda is future, irrotational and Born rigid: its rest slices lambda=const have fixed Euclidean induced metric. Its acceleration one-form is a-flat=[k(lambda)/N]d xi, and d(a-flat)=[1/(L_0^2N^2)]d lambda wedge d xi is nowhere zero. For a positive smooth f, the Killing equation for K=f n and Born rigidity imply d log f=a-flat, impossible because d^2 log f=0. Thus no positive smooth multiple of this n is Killing even locally; irrotational Born rigidity does not force a Killing rescaling. The Rindler congruence is not this counterexample: rho n=partial_theta is Killing for its theta-independent metric. The rotational classification of thm-sr-smooth-local-herglotz-noether is preserved; this example concerns its irrotational branch.
before.strategy: The hyperbolic identities give an orthonormal pair (e_0,e_1), with e_0'=k e_1 and e_1'=k e_0. The FTC defines z'=e_0. Differentiating Phi gives partial_lambda Phi=N e_0, partial_xi Phi=e_1 and the constant transverse vectors; at0 the derivative is invertible, so the choice-free smooth inverse-function theorem gives an injective local chart. Shrink to a coordinate box with |lambda|,|xi|<epsilon L_0 and epsilon<1 to ensure N>=1-epsilon^2>0. The metric follows directly; its rest-slice metric is lambda-independent, so theta=0, and its rest distribution is the lambda foliation, so omega=0. Its Christoffel/flat-coordinate derivative gives a=(k/N)partial_xi, hence a-flat=(k/N)d xi. Differentiate k/(1+k xi) in lambda: k'/N^2=1/(L_0^2N^2), proving the displayed nonclosed acceleration form. For Born-rigid n, sym nabla n=-n-flat sym-tensor a-flat. The equation L_{f n}eta=0 is n-flat sym-tensor(df-f a-flat)=0; evaluation twice on n and once on n plus a rest vector forces df-f a-flat=0, hence d log f=a-flat. Applying d and the exterior-square-zero theorem contradicts the everywhere nonzero displayed two-form. This replaces the false Rindler counterexample while preserving the full intended claim. Its explicit local construction has no global quotient, tube completeness or material-model assumption, and uses no choice principle.

before.title: Causal reachability, causal futures and pasts, causal diamonds, and reachability by future causal paths in affine Minkowski space
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model) and write Cbar^+ := cl(C^+) and Cbar^- := cl(C^-) for the closed future and past cones of the time orientation; these are the convex cones with Cbar^+ = C^+ union {0}, Cbar^- = C^- union {0} and Cbar^+ intersect Cbar^- = {0} (def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets, lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components). This definition fixes the following objects. (a) Causal and chronological reachability. For events p,q in A set p <=q iff q - p is in Cbar^+ and p <q iff q - p is in C^+; the first is read 'q is causally reachable from p' and the second 'q is strictly (chronologically) reachable from p'. (b) Futures and pasts. J^+(p) := {q : p <= q} = p + Cbar^+, I^+(p) := {q : p < q} = p + C^+, J^-(p) := {q : q <= p} = p + Cbar^- and I^-(p) := {q : q < p} = p + C^-; p lies in J^+(p) intersect J^-(p) and in neither I^+(p) nor I^-(p). (c) Causal diamonds. For events p,q in A with p <= q the causal diamond of the ordered pair (p,q) is the set J^+(p) intersect J^-(q). (d) Reachability by future causal paths. A piecewise C^1 future causal path is a piecewise C^1 curve x: [a,b] -> A (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline) whose one-sided tangents at every point of [a,b] are future causal (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). For events p,q in A say that q is reachable from p by a future causal path when p = q, or when p is not q and there are real numbers a < b and a piecewise C^1 future causal path x: [a,b] -> A with x(a) = p and x(b) = q; write R^+(p) for the set of events reachable from p in this sense. (e) Conventions and scope. All objects are defined from the affine structure, the form eta and the time orientation alone; no chart, origin, spatial orientation of V or unit convention enters. The statement asserts no property of these objects: the reflexivity of <= is (b), while transitivity of <=, the identification R^+(p) = J^+(p), the antisymmetry 'p <= q and q <= p imply p = q', the monotonicity of inertial coordinate time and the invariance under proper orthochronous affine Lorentz maps are proved later on this page (lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion, thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence, lem-sr-spacelike-pairs-have-frame-dependent-time-order). before.title: Parallel future null displacements compose to a future null displacement
before.statement: Worked computation in the chart x of an inertial frame. Let v := (1,1,0,0) and w := (2,2,0,0) be coordinate columns with respect to the basis of the frame. (a) v and w are future null: eta(v,v) = -1 + 1 = 0, eta(w,w) = -4 + 4 = 0, and both have positive time component; w = 2v, so the two directions are parallel. before.title: The displacement of a future timelike worldline is future timelike
before.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: [a,b] -> A be a future timelike worldline with a < b that is piecewise C^1 with partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b and satisfies the corner hypothesis (H) of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time. Put p := x(a), q := x(b) and d := q - p. Then d is future timelike. More precisely, writing xi^a := x_A^a o x for the coordinate path of the chart x_A of any inertial frame, xi^0(b) - xi^0(a) > 0 and |xi_vec(b) - xi_vec(a)| < xi^0(b) - xi^0(a), where |.| is the Euclidean spatial norm of def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame. Consequently p is not equal to q, the number sqrt(-eta(d,d)) is a positive real number, and in every inertial chart the time component of d is positive and dominates the Euclidean norm of its spatial part, which is exactly the coordinate description of future timelikeness in that chart. No completeness, compactness beyond the given compact interval, or choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Proof in the chart of an arbitrary inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Let xi := x_A o x; by def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline (a) each xi^a is, on every open piece, differentiable with derivative the corresponding component of E^{-1}(x'(s)) (E the frame isomorphism), and by (H) this derivative extends continuously to the closed piece. Hence on each closed piece [s_{i-1},s_i] the real functions xi^a are continuous and have continuously extendable derivatives, and the future timelikeness of x reads, in coordinates, (xi^{0'})^2 - |xi_vec'|^2 = -eta(x',x') > 0 with xi^{0'} > 0, i.e. xi^{0'} > |xi_vec'| >= 0 pointwise on the open piece (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components gives the coordinate description of the future cone). Increments: for the real-valued functions xi^a on a closed piece with continuously extended derivative f_i^a, put F_i^a(t) := integral_{s_{i-1}}^{t} f_i^a; by thm-ftc-first-part F_i^a is differentiable on the closed piece with (F_i^a)' = f_i^a, so xi^a - F_i^a is continuous on the closed piece and has zero derivative on its interior, hence is constant on the piece by cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant; therefore xi^a(s_i) - xi^a(s_{i-1}) = integral_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i} f_i^a. Summing over the finitely many pieces and using thm-additivity-over-subintervals gives xi^a(b) - xi^a(a) = integral over [a,b] of the piecewise-defined derivative, assembled componentwise (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, def-oriented-integral). Strict positivity of the time increment: xi^{0'} - |xi_vec'| is continuous on each closed piece and strictly positive on its interior, hence its integral over a nondegenerate piece is positive (thm-nonnegative-continuous-with-zero-integral-vanishes applied to each closed piece after extension by continuity, or monotonicity of the integral thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral with strict pointwise positivity); summing gives xi^0(b) - xi^0(a) > 0 and, by the norm inequality for vector-valued integrals on each piece (thm-norm-inequality-for-the-vector-valued-integral) together with the triangle inequality for the Euclidean norm (cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm), |xi_vec(b) - xi_vec(a)| = |sum_i integral f_i^vec| <= sum_i |integral f_i^vec| <= sum_i integral |f_i^vec| < sum_i integral f_i^0 = xi^0(b) - xi^0(a). This is precisely the coordinate description of future timelikeness for d in this frame, so d is future timelike (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components, def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors); the frame was arbitrary, and the conclusion is frame-independent. before.title: The endpoint bound for proper time and the maximality of the straight worldline in affine Minkowski space
before.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: [a,b] -> A be a future timelike worldline with a < b that is piecewise C^1 with partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b and satisfies the corner hypothesis (H) of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time, with total proper time Delta tau(x) of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time. Put p := x(a), q := x(b) and T := sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)), a positive real number (lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline). Then: (i) Endpoint bound: c Delta tau(x) <= T. (ii) Equality case: c Delta tau(x) = T if and only if x is a strictly increasing reparametrization of the straight segment from p to q, that is: there is a continuous strictly increasing surjection sigma: [a,b] -> [0,1] with sigma(a) = 0 and sigma(b) = 1, C^1 on every open piece of a partition of [a,b] satisfying (H), with sigma'(s) > 0 at every point of each open piece and finite one-sided limits at the partition points, such that x(s) = p + sigma(s)(q - p) for every s in [a,b]; equivalently x'(s) is a positive multiple of q - p at every point at which x is differentiable. (iii) Strictness: if the image of x is not contained in the straight segment {p + lambda(q-p) : 0 <= lambda <= 1}, then c Delta tau(x) < T; in particular, if x is piecewise inertial and its piece tangents d_1,...,d_m are not all positive multiples of one another (equivalently, its image is not contained in the straight segment), then the inequality is strict, while a piecewise inertial itinerary whose piece tangents are all positive multiples of one another has the straight segment as image and attains the bound. (iv) Straight worldlines attain the bound: for the inertial worldline x_s(s) := p + ((s-a)/(b-a))(q-p) one has c Delta tau(x_s) = T, in agreement with the straight-segment value of def-sr-proper-time; more generally every worldline whose image is the straight segment and which is traversed in the future direction attains the bound. (v) Scope: the theorem concerns the affine Minkowski model with a fixed positive constant c; it is a statement about the curve class (H) only, it does not identify proper time with any clock reading, and it asserts nothing about maximality of geodesics in curved spacetimes or in Lorentzian manifolds with different global structure.

For (ii), equality in the sum means sum_i integral h_i = 0 with each integral >= 0, hence integral h_i = 0 for every i, hence h_i vanishes identically on each closed piece (thm-nonnegative-continuous-with-zero-integral-vanishes), hence xi_vec' = 0 on every open piece; then xi_vec is constant on each closed piece (cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant) and, by continuity at the corners, on all of [a,b]; consequently x(s) = o + xi^0(s) e_0 + xi_vec(a) = p + (xi^0(s) - xi^0(a)) e_0 = p + sigma(s)(q - p) with sigma(s) := (xi^0(s) - xi^0(a))/T. The function sigma is continuous, strictly increasing (xi^{0'} > 0 pointwise, so xi^0 is strictly increasing on each piece by cor-mean-value-theorem applied to the closed piece and by additivity), surjective onto [0,1] because sigma(a) = 0 and sigma(b) = (xi^0(b) - xi^0(a))/T = T/T = 1, and on each open piece it is C^1 with derivative xi^{0'}/T > 0 and finite one-sided limits by (H). Conversely, if x has the displayed form, then x' = sigma'(q - p) with sigma' > 0, so -eta(x',x') = (sigma')^2 T^2 and the integrand is sigma' T; the total proper time is sum_i T integral sigma' = T(sigma(b) - sigma(a)) = T by the same per-piece increment argument. This proves (ii). (iii) is the contrapositive of (ii): if the image is not contained in the straight segment, x is not such a reparametrization, so equality fails, while (i) gives <=. (iv) is the computation x' = (q-p)/(b-a) with -eta = T^2/(b-a)^2 and integral over [a,b] equal to T, or clause (ii) with the affine sigma(s) = (s-a)/(b-a). before.title: Same-endpoint clock comparison: the inertial clock is slowest to age
before.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions the postulates post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis, and let c and the SI conventions be those of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let p and q be events with q - p future timelike, put T := sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) > 0, and let x_s: [a,b] -> A be the straight (inertial) future timelike worldline from p to q, x_s(s) := p + ((s-a)/(b-a))(q-p). Let x: [a,b] -> A be a piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline from p to q satisfying the corner hypothesis (H) of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time, with total proper time Delta tau(x). Then, as conditional statements about ideal clocks of the adopted model and not about any actual apparatus: (i) an ideal clock carried along x_s from p to q reads between the parameter values a and b the time c^{-1} T; (ii) an ideal clock carried along x from p to q reads Delta tau(x), and Delta tau(x) <= c^{-1} T, with equality if and only if x is a strictly increasing reparametrization of the straight segment from p to q in the sense of thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum (ii); (iii) if x is piecewise inertial (def-sr-inertial-and-piecewise-inertial-worldline) and its image is not contained in the straight segment from p to q, then Delta tau(x) < c^{-1} T strictly, so among ideal clocks carried between the same two events along future timelike piecewise C^1 histories of the class (H) the straight inertial clock records the largest reading, and every history whose image is not the straight segment records a strictly smaller one; (iv) the two numbers Delta tau(x) and c^{-1} T are determined by the parametrized histories and the model's conversion constant alone: the integrand sqrt(-eta(x',x')) of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time involves no chart, so the comparison is a definite pair of clock readings attached to the same pair of endpoint events and involves no simultaneity convention. Scope and qualification: the statement inherits the idealizations of its postulates (ideal pointlike clocks with no acceleration-dependent reading term, prescribed histories, flat classical spacetime, the fixed conversion constant c); it asserts no measurement outcome, contains no statistical inference, and carries no claim that real clocks or the physical world are exactly described by the model. The conclusion is conditional on the named postulates and does not follow from the geometry alone.
before.strategy: Conditional deduction from the adopted postulates; the mathematical engine is thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum. (i) The straight history has constant tangent (q-p)/(b-a), so its proper-time function has the constant rate c^{-1} T/(b-a) (def-sr-proper-time straight-segment value) and the clock hypothesis of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light identifies the reading with that integral, giving c^{-1} T. (ii) For a piecewise C^1 history with finitely many kinks the reading is the total proper time of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time (post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis (ii) states the clock hypothesis for exactly this class, referring to the piecewise integral, and post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light fixes the reading for the C^1 pieces); the bound, equality case and strictness are clauses (i)-(iii) of thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum.
